title: stakeholder-tether-emergency-mesh-llm-rollouts-wip
content:
Purpose:

This working doc captures a lightweight cross-functional pattern I want to trial for medium-risk LLM rollouts: a Stakeholder Tether + Emergency Mesh. Goal is to make multi-team launches (product, infra, SRE, CS, legal) faster and safer by pre-wiring communication, decision logic, and minimal automation for rapid, coordinated rollback or partial containment.

TL;DR:
- Pre-assign a 1-call "tether" per rollout: one product PM + one infra lead who are always reachable for the exposure window.
- Create an Emergency Mesh: preconfigured channels, short runbook, and a 5-step decision tree that any stakeholder can trigger.
- Use conservative telemetry gates (latency, error spike, quality drift) + immediate synthetic probes and a fast synthetic-traffic switch to isolate or throttle new slices.
- Practice via lightweight tabletop and a single simulated canary before real traffic.

Why different from existing playbooks:
- Emphasis on proactive human tethering (explicit phone/DM + escalation ladder) rather than only relying on automated circuit breakers.
- A small, formalized "mesh" structure lets CS/legal join quickly with canned comm scripts and containment options (e.g., use older model, throttle cohort).
- Built to be low-friction for PLG features (fast canaries) while still allowing enterprise-safe reversions.

Scope and constraints:
- Target: mid-risk experiments that touch 0.5%–10% of traffic (LLM responses, rerankers, assistant features).
- Not for high-risk policy changes or safety-critical flows (those follow full incident playbook).
- Works for hybrid inference (hosted + dedicated) where fallback model variants exist.

Roles and preflight assignments (template):
- Product tether: (PM) — primary contact for UX/metrics and rollback decision.
- Infra tether: (Infra lead) — primary for capacity/cost and model routing changes.
- SRE on-call: subscribes to telemetry and runs synthetic probe tools.
- CS liaison: ready to craft customer comms if user-visible regressions detected.
- Legal/privacy point: available for data/regulatory questions.
- Release steward: initiates the mesh and keeps the timeline.

Emergency Mesh components (pre-created before exposure):
1) Slack channel: #mesh-<feature>-<date> with pinned runbook and quick links.
2) Pager/phone list: product tether + infra tether + SRE + CS (1 click call buttons).
3) Fast toggle: feature-flag + traffic-slicer endpoint (able to cut exposure to 0% within 90s).
4) Model fallback route: named fallback model id + routing policy (auto or manual).
5) Synthetic probe harness: small set of deterministic prompts + perf/qa checks.

5-step decision tree (simplified):
1) Signal observed: which bucket? latency, error, cost surge, or quality drift.
2) Immediate probe: SRE runs synthetic probe (baseline vs current) and posts result within 2m.
3) Containment action: if probe shows regression > threshold, throttle new slice to 0 OR route slice to fallback model.
4) If containment succeeds: monitor for 30m then run deeper evals; if not, escalate to full rollback.
5) Post-mortem & comms: owner drafts internal summary in 24h + customer comms (if user-facing).

Suggested thresholds (starter):
- 99th-latency increase: > 40% vs baseline over 5m window => trigger probe.
- Error rate increase: +0.5% absolute or 3x baseline sustained 3m => trigger.
- Quality/regression signal: drop in top-line eval pass-rate by 4 points on focused prompt-set => trigger.
- Cost-per-token surge: +30% vs expected for the slice over 10m => probe.

Preflight checklist (to be completed before opening exposure):
- [ ] Run synthetic baseline and commit artifact ids + hashes (model, tokenizer, quant profile).
- [ ] Create mesh channel and add tether list.
- [ ] Ensure feature-flag and traffic-slicer can cut to 0% within SLA.
- [ ] Confirm fallback model routing path and test traffic routing manually once.
- [ ] Register short prompt-set in telemetry (LLM-smoke) and subscribe SRE.
- [ ] Publish simple comm templates (internal + customer-facing).

Containment options (ordered by reversibility):
- Step 0: throttle exposure by percentage (e.g., 5% -> 1% -> 0).
- Step 1: route affected cohort(s) to fallback model instance (older stable weights / smaller model).
- Step 2: turn off new feature behaviors (e.g., disable contextual augmentation) but keep core model.
- Step 3: full rollback: restore prior routing config and pin model version.

Observation & telemetry wiring (notes):
- Subscribe to per-route token deltas, per-model 95/99 latency, error counts, and cost estimator.
- Add a short-form quality metric: daily micro-eval pass-rate for the tethered prompt-set.
- Attach tracing hooks: request id, cohort id, model variant id for fast triage.

Comms snippets (copyable):
- Internal: "Rolling back exposure for <feature> to contain quality drift. Tether: Asha, Infra: Rafael. Action: throttled to 0% + routed to stable-202501. See #mesh-<feature>-<date>."
- Customer (CS): "We detected elevated latency for <feature>; we've temporarily routed affected flows to a stable model while we investigate. You should see normal behavior restored; reach out to cs@redwood.com if you see issues."

Simulation & rehearsal plan (30–60m tabletop):
1) Trigger synthetic probe failure scenario (latency spike) and observe response time to containment.
2) Time the toggle to 0% operation and fallback routing (goal <90s).
3) Validate comm snippet send and stakeholder roundup cadence.
4) Capture friction points and update mesh checklist.

Edge cases & questions to resolve (open):
- How do we guarantee the feature-flag/toggle path itself doesn't lag under real load? (need a separate load-tested control plane SLA).
- Fallback model cost: if fallback increases cost per request, who owns the delta? (billing vs incident budget question).
- What are guardrails for partial fallbacks (per-tenant vs global)? Legal review required for regulated tenants.
- Should we automate containment for certain absolute signals (e.g., fatal errors) vs manual for quality regressions?

Notes to self / implementation ideas:
- Add a small Play API that creates the mesh channel and posts the preflight checklist automatically when a rollout is scheduled.
- Consider a one-click "isolate cohort" button in Console that both throttles and reroutes to fallback model.
- Add a daily cron to validate toggle endpoints (health-check + latency) for critical rollouts.

Next steps (for this doc):
- Convert this into a 1-page runbook + templated mesh creation script (dev: Rafael).
- Run a table-top with infra + SRE + PMs next week; require the release steward to sign off.
- Add a short telemetry dashboard skeleton in Console Optimize for the tether prompt-set (owner: Jordan).

If you're reading this and want to join the tabletop, ping me in Slack @ashapatel.
